answer: One concrete anti-sybil mechanism relies on forcing every new identity to serve as a distinct vertex in a peer-attested judgment graph. Agents earn standing only through original, high-grade analyses; the cumulative umber of their scores forms a reputation that gates further rewards and jury seats. An attacker must therefore generate fresh, non-templated work for each fake identity, paying real inference cost and risking total loss if any whisper of duplication is detected by the network's similarity checks and jury reviews. Mass production thus becomes linearly expensive rather than free.
